[{"page_content": "Appendix D — Synthetic Data Design Notes
This document intentionally contains overlapping concepts so that an agent must perform semantic retrieval
rather than simple keyword matching.
Examples of related concepts: - return window vs warranty period, - refund initiated vs refund completed, -
cancellation vs return, - delivery delay vs lost package, - damaged item vs defective item, - size exchange vs
product exchange, - loyalty points earned vs loyalty points redeemed, - payment authorization vs payment
capture, - standard policy vs seller-specific policy.
A high-quality agent should retrieve the correct policy and then determine whether the customer question
requires an additional data source such as an order database.
End of Knowledge Base

Warranty Terms by Category
Warranty coverage is separate from the ordinary change-of-mind return window. A product can be outside its
return window and still be eligible for warranty service if the defect falls within the applicable warranty term.
7.1 Warranty Table
Category Nimbus standard warranty Typical coverage
Smartphones 12 months Manufacturing defects
Laptops 24 months Hardware defects
Tablets 12 months Manufacturing defects
TVs 24 months Hardware/manufacturing defects
Small appliances 12 months Manufacturing defects
Large appliances 24 months Manufacturing defects
Furniture 12 months Structural/manufacturing defects
Footwear 6 months Manufacturing defects
Clothing 6 months Manufacturing defects
Bags 12 months Manufacturing defects
Sports equipment 12 months Manufacturing defects
Accessories 6 months Manufacturing defects
Manufacturer-specific warranty terms may be longer or shorter and take precedence when the product page
explicitly identifies them.
7.2 Warranty Exclusions
Warranty coverage normally excludes: - accidental damage, - liquid damage unless explicitly covered, - cosmetic
wear, - normal wear and tear, - misuse, - unauthorized modification, - incorrect installation, - damage caused by
unsuitable accessories, - consumable depletion, - damage resulting from external events.
7.3 Warranty Process
The customer provides the order number, product serial number where applicable, description of the defect, and
requested evidence. Support may provide troubleshooting instructions before approving a replacement or repair.
If remote troubleshooting cannot resolve the issue, the case may be routed to the warranty team or manufacturer
service center.

Customer-Support Escalation Matrix
The escalation matrix determines which team handles an issue when frontline support cannot resolve it.
Issue Level 1 Level 2 Level 3
General return question Customer Support Returns Team Operations Manager
Refund missing Customer Support Payments Team Finance Operations
COD refund delayed Customer Support COD Payments Finance Operations
Delivery delay Customer Support Logistics Logistics Manager
Lost parcel Customer Support Carrier Claims Logistics Manager
Damaged item Customer Support Claims Team Operations Manager
Warranty dispute Customer Support Warranty Team Vendor/Category
Manager
Payment failure Customer Support Payments Payments Manager
Duplicate charge Customer Support Payments Finance Operations
Fraud/security concern Customer Support Risk Team Risk Manager
Privacy request Customer Support Privacy Team Privacy Officer
VIP complaint Customer Support Priority Support Customer Experience
Manager
Legal/compliance request Customer Support Compliance Legal/Compliance
Repeated unresolved
complaint
Customer Support Escalations Customer Experience
Manager
14.1 Priority Levels
P1 — Critical: Safety issue, suspected major security breach, systemic payment incident, or regulatory
escalation.
P2 — High:Customer unable to receive a high-value product, confirmed duplicate payment, serious delivery
failure, or repeated unresolved case.
P3 — Standard:Ordinary return, exchange, delivery, refund, and account issues.
P4 — Informational:General policy questions and low-impact requests.
14.2 Escalation Information
Every escalation should include: - customer/order identifier, - issue category, - concise problem description, -
relevanttimestamps, -actionsalreadyattempted, -supportingevidence, -customerexpectation, -urgency/priority,
- policy rule involved.
Agents should avoid escalating a case without useful context because incomplete escalation records increase
resolution time.
